bounded_statement: The report's selected result computes the occurrence rate on the retained post-screening subset (9 detections / 36 retained pointings = 25.00%) but labels and interprets that rate as the detection rate of the complete planned set of 48 pointings, explicitly applying it to the full observing plan including the 12 screened-out pointings, while the governing task and the report's own protocol-status section declare the complete planned set as the scientific target. The complete-set rate supported by the same accounting would use the 48-pointing denominator (9/48 = 18.75%), so the headline 25.00% overstates the complete-domain rate by attributing a retained-subset quantity to the complete domain.

counterevidence_considered.description: Against my demonstrated-issue verdict: the report transparently discloses that the denominator is the 36 retained pointings and that the 12 removed pointings are excluded, so a careful reader can reconstruct what was computed. This transparency does not cure the issue, because the headline result and the interpretation section still attribute the subset rate to the complete planned set of 48 pointings and apply it to the removed pointings.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the verdict three ways. First, I considered whether the retained subset could legitimately be the declared domain: the task, the report title, the subject-area section, and the protocol-status section all declare the complete planned set of 48 pointings as the scientific target, and the report states no amendment exists, so the subset is not an authorized redefinition of the domain. Second, I considered whether the disclosure of the 36-pointing denominator makes the labeling merely descriptive rather than a complete-domain claim: the interpretation section defeats this by stating the 25.00% rate 'is reported as the detection rate of the complete planned set' and 'is applied to the full observing plan, including the 12 pointings that the screening step removed', which is an affirmative projection of the subset rate onto units it was not computed over. Third, I checked the arithmetic independently: 9/36 = 25.00% is the retained-subset rate, while the complete-set rate under the supplied planned-unit accounting is 9/48 = 18.75%, confirming the reported figure is the subset quantity, not a complete-domain quantity under any denominator convention visible in the files. All three falsification routes failed, so the issue stands as demonstrated.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py computes the proportion with the retained-subset denominator (proportion = Fraction(events, retained)) and then writes report text that attributes this subset rate to the complete planned set of 48 pointings ('detection rate for the complete planned set of 48 pointings', 'applied to the full observing plan, including the 12 pointings that the screening step removed'), with no protocol amendment authorizing the domain change.
